title: Adrian Rollini's New Yorkers offer and the choice to join Whiteman
summary: Rollini tried to take the Goldkette men to the New Yorker Hotel; Challis chose Whiteman and could not persuade Bix and Trumbauer to follow.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I stayed with the band until the end of that engagement. Then another weekend, down comes Rollini, Adrian, and he said that he wanted to know the same thing, "What are you guys going to do?" And he wants to take all the guys but he won't have Steve Brown. Steve Brown was a big feature in our band, because he plays bass himself, but the bass fiddle is out.
So now he wants Bix and I think he wanted Farrar, it seems Farrar was in that; but Farrar was going to work with Shilkret anyway, and Shulkret (phonetic) was in doing -- what they
call transcriptions and he was big wheel and power down at the Victor and he had four or five radio shows, so he was -- you know, he would be the guy for a guy like Farrar to go with. And he did.

So what's his name took -- he didn't take Itzy Itzy Riscoll -- he didn't know what Itzy was going to do. Let's see, who else -- Chauncey, well he could have used Chauncey too. He went with the New Yorkers, and then he wanted me to go with the New Yorkers and play, back on the saxophone.
Had you played at all in these years?
Not even just to fool around.

Oh, once in awhile, I'd practice and blow a couple of tunes. I filled in one night when Trumbauer had the mole taken off under his eye. He used to have a mole there and he had it taken off. I played, but it was only one night.

So he wanted me to play and arrange, but the difference of playing with that band, the guys would be great, but the difference of playing with them. He was going -- he got the New Yorker job, the Goldkette band didn't get it and Whiteman didn't want it. So this is what these guys had to look forward to, and he also said he could get them a lot of recordings, that he did a lot of recording himself.
So to me there was no choice. I thought it would

be an advancement for me to go with the Whiteman band. There were more instruments, arrangements, a lot more possibilities in the band and as far as Trumbauer and Bix were concerned, it would be logical for them to go with Rollini, but I tried to get them to go with Paul, and no, they didn't want to go there.
